title: Registry match rate reported as 79.3% when the real Manhattan rate is 99.5%
how_found: Reviewing REGISTRY_REPORT.json against the source counts
root_cause: Percentages were computed over all 56476 rows including 11482 context-borough buildings, which can never match a Manhattan-only NYC extract
fix: Report all-rows and Manhattan-only figures separately; Manhattan is the headline number
verification: matched_pct_manhattan = 99.49 across 44994 rows; 42627 high confidence

title: pluto_joined_pct_manhattan reported 99.49%, identical to the footprint match rate
how_found: Two adjacent metrics in the same report had byte-identical values, which is not plausible
root_cause: Presence of bbl was used as the PLUTO-join test, but bbl comes from the NYC footprint, not from PLUTO
fix: Test building_class instead, which is only ever set from a matched PLUTO lot
verification: pluto_joined_pct_manhattan = 91.97, matching the independently measured 92.0%

title: 42.1% of all buildings classified as brownstone_rowhouse
how_found: Distribution sanity check against the real city; no district in Manhattan is 42% rowhouse
root_cause: NYC building class C is walk-up apartments (tenements), not rowhouses. 12721 C-class buildings were labelled brownstone by an area heuristic
fix: Split on the C sub-class: C0/C3 and small C2/C5 are converted rowhouses, C1/C4/C6/C8 are tenements, C7 is walk-up-over-stores. Verified against measured Manhattan medians per sub-class
verification: Manhattan brownstone 20.7% (9321). Independent envelope test (footprint <150 m2 and <=5 floors) gives 36.9%, so the classifier is conservative not inflated

title: beaux_arts_civic over-assigned at 7.9%
how_found: Same distribution check
root_cause: Any pre-war O-class office below 11 floors fell through to the Beaux-Arts fallback
fix: Route the small pre-war commercial fallback to mixed_use_avenue; reserve Beaux-Arts for the civic classes N/P/Q/J/Y/Z
verification: beaux_arts_civic now 2.6% of Manhattan (1173)

title: Geometry fallback assigned brownstone to anything under 260 m2 with <=5 floors
how_found: Reviewing the fallback path while fixing P2-003
root_cause: 260 m2 is roughly twice a real NYC rowhouse footprint, so tenement-scale blocks qualified
fix: Tighten to 150 m2, the measured p90 of confirmed rowhouse footprints (136 m2)
verification: Fallback brownstones in Manhattan fell from an estimated 604 to 536; brownstone footprint p50 = 93 m2, p90 = 136 m2

title: District assignment badly wrong: Upper West Side 1071 buildings, East Village 70, Chinatown 42, East Harlem 5016
how_found: Cross-tabulating archetypes by district and finding implausible district sizes
root_cause: Phase 1 district_of() used latitude bands split east/west at a fixed local-x. Manhattan is rotated ~29 degrees, so a fixed x drifts across the avenues as latitude changes
fix: Replace with point-in-polygon against NYC 2020 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas (9nt8-h7nd). Implemented as a Phase 2 enrichment because Phase 1 scripts are frozen; the old label is kept in district_coarse
verification: 44724 of 44994 (99.40%) assigned, all 38 NTAs used. UWS now 4629 across 3 NTAs, East Village 2405, Chinatown 1109, Stuyvesant Town 84 (correct, it is 110 buildings on superblocks)

title: verify_baseline.py failed on every rebuild
how_found: Running the freeze verifier after a clean rebuild
root_cause: Binary outputs (.blend, .mp4, .png) embed timestamps, so hashing them as a pass/fail gate can never pass
fix: Split tracked groups into enforced (scripts, caches, derived data) and recorded (binaries, docs, renders). Only enforced groups gate the build
verification: verify_baseline.py passes on a clean rebuild; drift in recorded groups is reported, not failed

title: 270 Manhattan buildings fall outside every NTA polygon
how_found: District assignment report
root_cause: They sit on piers and landfill beyond the NTA shoreline, which follows the legal waterfront rather than built structures
fix: Not yet fixed. They retain their Phase 1 label and are flagged nta_type=unassigned so they are visible rather than silently mislabelled
verification: 0.60% of Manhattan; all are waterfront structures. Audited 2026-08-05: 270 confirmed, 243 Inwood, 263 of 270 far from the core; the honest fix is the unassigned label, keep open as won't-fix-by-design

title: Manhattan buildings classified by geometry alone with no city data behind the decision
how_found: archetype_source distribution
root_cause: They have no PLUTO match, mostly small rear structures, unaddressed lots and new construction
fix: Partly fixed by P2-011 (OSM tags now cover office/apartments/retail). The remainder are recorded as archetype_source=geometry so the gap is auditable
verification: Manhattan geometry-only fell from 3570 to a residue after the OSM-tag path took 3193 rows citywide. Audited 2026-08-05: residue now 277 of 44,994 (0.6%); 215 are <300 m2 rear/small structures, 17 are >=60 m (30 Hudson Yards at 395 m is genuinely new construction with no lot record yet); acceptable residue, keep open

title: 152 towers between 90 m and 150 m classified as early_skyscraper_masonry regardless of era, including Citigroup Center (1978)
how_found: Spot-checking the ten tallest buildings in the browser runtime
root_cause: The geometry fallback gated the modern eras at h>=150 m, so a 100 m 2005 tower fell past both modern branches into the pre-war archetype. Height was deciding style instead of era
fix: Restructure the tower branch so era decides: >=1985 glass, >=1945 postwar slab, >=1925 art deco, else early tower. Unknown year on a 150 m+ building means no lot record, which almost always means new construction
verification: Tall geometry-decided early_skyscraper_masonry fell from 152 to 19. Spot check: Empire State art deco, Chrysler art deco, Flatiron early tower, Woolworth early tower, Seagram postwar slab, Citigroup postwar slab, One WTC glass

title: Supertalls with no PLUTO row fell through to the geometry ladder even though OSM tagged them correctly
how_found: Central Park Tower (472 m) and One Manhattan West (303 m) both showed archetype_source=geometry despite a high-confidence NYC footprint match
root_cause: New construction gets a BIN and a BBL but no PLUTO lot record yet. The OSM-tag fallback only covered church/school/hospital/hotel/warehouse/transit/garage, so office/apartments/residential/retail tags were discarded
fix: Extend the OSM-tag fallback into the shared office and residential lineage helpers, so the tag path and the building-class path cannot drift apart
verification: 3193 rows now decided by osm_tag+year+floors. Central Park Tower -> contemporary luxury residential, Citigroup Center -> postwar slab, 30 Rockefeller Plaza -> art deco

title: The browser kept serving a stale city after the classifier was re-run
how_found: Verifying the archetype fix through the running app: the page reported Citigroup Center as art_deco_tower while the CSV on disk said postwar_office_slab
root_cause: The dev-server middleware set Cache-Control max-age=3600 on every mount, including the small runtime payload that is rewritten on every classifier run
fix: Cache /tiles/ (large, rarely rebuilt) and set no-store on /data/ (small, rewritten constantly)
verification: A cache-bypassing refetch and a normal reload now agree with the CSV on all six spot-checked landmarks

title: Condominium BBLs do not join to PLUTO, so recent towers lose their lot attributes
how_found: Central Park Tower matched a NYC footprint at 1.4 m with a 0.874 area ratio and still had an empty building_class
root_cause: PLUTO stores condominium lots under the mappluto BBL carried on the building footprint; the registry joined only on base_bbl, which for condos is the pre-condo parcel PLUTO no longer lists. Measured: 3,536 footprints have base_bbl != mappluto_bbl; base_bbl joins PLUTO on 41,705/45,194 (92.28%), mappluto_bbl on 45,143 (99.89%)
fix: 41_build_registry.py now carries bbl_mappluto alongside bbl, tries base first then falls back to mappluto, and records which one joined in bbl_source. Full chain re-run; registry and demand regenerated; byte-identical across two runs
verification: pluto_joined_manhattan 41,381 -> 44,733 (91.97% -> 99.42%), 3,353 joined via mappluto. Recovered: Central Park Tower 472 m, 432 Park Avenue 426 m, 53 West 53 320 m, 35 Hudson Yards 304.8 m, 520 5th Avenue 304.8 m, One Manhattan West 303 m. Demand field: 3,407 cells changed, p99 day scale +24.4%, eve +41.6%. 30 rows still unjoined (18 pseudo-BBLs ending 9999, 12 special keys)

title: Every building rendered near-black once the facade shader was applied
how_found: First street-level capture from the running app
root_cause: The shader multiplied the palette colour by diffuseColor, which three had already multiplied by COLOR_0. Two dark values multiplied together: 0.3 * 0.3 = 0.09
fix: Use the palette as the authority on colour and keep COLOR_0 only as a +-8% per-building tint
verification: Street and aerial captures show lit masonry with readable window openings

title: The ground rendered as sky: no landmass, water or roads anywhere
how_found: First aerial capture showed buildings floating on blue
root_cause: manhattan_base.glb holds every object whose name carried no tile suffix - the landmass, the water plane, the bridges - and the tile regex only matched manhattan_NN_NN.glb, so it was never in the manifest
fix: Add it to the tile list flagged always-resident, and make the streamer never unload an always tile
verification: 119 tiles resident instead of 118; land, rivers and parks visible in every aerial capture

title: Ground, roads, parks and trees exported to glTF as pure white and blew out to a featureless white plane
how_found: Aerial capture after the base tile was added; the island was white from horizon to horizon
root_cause: Five Phase 1 materials build their colour in a Blender node graph (noise -> colour ramp -> Base Color). glTF has no equivalent, so the exporter writes baseColorFactor = white and expects a texture that does not exist
fix: New Phase 2 export script flattens those five graphs to the midpoint of their colour ramps in memory only, then re-exports. Phase 1 scripts and the .blend on disk are untouched
verification: MAT_land #3f3e3c, MAT_asphalt #2f2f31, MAT_park #3a522a, MAT_tree #304622 in the browser; the island reads as asphalt and green

title: Every ground-floor treatment the classifier assigns was invisible
how_found: Looking for storefronts at street level and finding none
root_cause: Phase 1 raised the land plane to 12 m to cure depth speckle, but buildings still extrude from 0, so the bottom 12 m of every building is buried - including the entire ground-floor band the shader draws
fix: Measure facade height from the street: read LAND_LEVEL out of blender_common.py into city.json and subtract it in the shader
verification: Storefronts, sign fascias and bulkheads visible at street level; floor lines now align with the pavement

title: A corrected re-export appeared to have no effect in the browser
how_found: Re-exported all 119 tiles with fixed materials, reloaded, and saw the identical white ground
root_cause: The dev server sends Cache-Control max-age=3600 on /tiles/, which is correct for a large immutable asset but means a rebuild is invisible until the cache expires
fix: Record each tile's mtime in the manifest and append it to the request URL, so a re-export changes the URL
verification: Flattened material colours reached the browser on the next reload

title: Storefront bands rendered as a solid bright blue stripe around the base of every building
how_found: Harlem street capture
root_cause: The ground floor was drawn as one large glass opening with the same sky-reflection term as an upper-floor window, and at a grazing angle the fresnel drove it to sky blue
fix: Draw the real stack - bulkhead, glass, sign fascia - and cut the sky reflection on shop glass, which is recessed and full of dark interior
verification: Storefronts read as recessed dark glazing with a fascia above

title: Evidence capture labelled harlem_rowhouses photographed the East River
how_found: Reviewing the captured PNG against its name
root_cause: Camera positions were written as hand-computed local metres and the Harlem one was wrong by about 3 km
fix: Define every shot as a real latitude and longitude and project it at capture time
verification: All ten shots land in the district they are named after

title: Draco quantized _bid so 83% of building ids arrived non-integer and picking returned a neighbour's record
how_found: Sampled 180925 _bid values straight off the loaded geometry after wiring the street layer
root_cause: glTF Draco export defaults export_draco_generic_quantization to 12 bits, and generic covers custom attributes. Over the 0-56475 id range that is a step of about 14, so ids were smeared by up to 9
fix: Raise generic quantization to 24 bits. _BID presence was already a regression requirement (R14); the value being exact now is too
verification: Worst id error fell from 0.5 (a step of ~14) to 0.0039. Five sample picks all returned exact integers and the correct building record

title: Every road, kerb and lane marking in the city was buried under the ground plane
how_found: Probing straight down from a street-level camera: the only hit was LAND_manhattan at y=12.407 when the blend file has its top at exactly 12.000
root_cause: Draco position quantization defaults to 14 bits spread across each mesh's own bounding box. LAND_manhattan spans 14.4 km, so the step is 0.88 m and a vertex authored at 12.00 landed at 12.407 - well above the 50 mm the roads sit proud of the land
fix: Raise position quantization to 20 bits: 14 mm on the 14.4 km land mesh, 1.3 mm on a 1.4 km tile
verification: Land now measures 11.993 (0.007 m error). A downward probe on 7 Ave returns ROADMARK 12.08 / ROAD 12.05 / LAND 11.993 in the correct order, and streets render

title: Sidewalk area came out at 34.65 km2 for a 59 km2 borough
how_found: Sanity-checking the street report against the size of Manhattan
root_cause: Two compounding errors: the fetch bbox around Manhattan also contains Long Island City, Williamsburg, Hoboken and the south Bronx; and the area sum counted only outer rings, so every block interior enclosed by a sidewalk ring was counted as pavement
fix: Filter by point-in-polygon against the city's own NTA polygons (shared scripts/phase2/nta.py), and subtract hole rings from the area
verification: 5202 polygons with 3854 holes, 6.97 km2 net - the right order for a borough with about 800 km of street frontage

title: Evidence shot named fifth_ave_34th photographed an empty plane from inside the Empire State Building's block
how_found: Comparing the shot to what a camera at 5th and 34th should see
root_cause: A latitude and longitude typed from memory lands mid-block about as often as it lands on a street, and 30 m of error matters when the street is 30 m wide
fix: Snap every street-level shot to the nearest drivable segment in the street graph and aim it along that segment
verification: All six street-level shots now stand on a carriageway looking down it

title: Capture placed the camera but every shot pointed wherever the camera was last left
how_found: Two consecutive shots came out with identical framing
root_cause: Controls.update() is what converts yaw and pitch into a camera quaternion, and it runs from the render loop - which the browser throttles to about 1 Hz in a hidden tab
fix: Set the quaternion directly in place(), and pump the streamers explicitly in settle() instead of relying on requestAnimationFrame
verification: Each shot now frames its own subject, and tiles for a new position load before the frame is taken

title: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center (1986 glass and steel) classified as prewar_masonry_apartment
how_found: Picking buildings in the runtime after the id fix made picking trustworthy; reproduced in the qa-integrity audit (building 19495)
root_cause: No NYC footprint match (match_confidence=none) and an uninformative OSM tag (building=yes), so the geometry ladder decided. The ladder never considered footprint scale: an 86,230 m2 floor plate is two city blocks, no apartment building is that wide, but 53.6 m height fell below the tower branch and the small-building branches, then landed on prewar apartment
fix: The geometry ladder now checks footprint >= 30,000 m2 after the tower branch: named large sheds classify as beaux_arts_civic, unnamed as warehouse. Only 4 Manhattan buildings (and 1 context row) exceed 30,000 m2, so the rule is surgical
verification: Javits is now beaux_arts_civic. The one unnamed context shed (32,011 m2, Jersey filler) is now warehouse instead of prewar apartment. No other building changed archetype

title: Every vehicle reported a 1.9 m length, collapsing car-following gaps
how_found: Printing the fleet dimensions after loading vehicles.glb: a bus came out 2.6 m long
root_cause: The glTF exporter maps Blender (x,y,z) to (x,z,-y). Bodies are authored along Blender +x, so after export length is the x extent and width is the z extent - they were read the other way round
fix: Swap the axes when measuring the bounding box
verification: sedan 4.80 x 1.92, bus 12.26 x 2.56, matching the authored dimensions

title: Instance paint tinted the glass and tyres along with the body
how_found: First traffic render: vehicles were uniformly pale with no visible glazing
root_cause: The paint-mask shader read a vInstanceColor varying, which three does not declare - its color_vertex chunk multiplies instanceColor into vColor instead
fix: Keep the raw COLOR_0 attribute in a vPaint varying and mix against vColor, which already carries the instance tint. Body panels are authored white so vColor is the paint; glass and tyres take vPaint's own rgb
verification: Vehicles now render in distinct colours with dark glazing, black tyres and red tail lamps; taxis are yellow with untinted glass

title: The outer lane of every avenue ran along the pavement
how_found: First traffic render at Times Square: cars driving on the sidewalk
root_cause: Lane offsets were stacked at a fixed 3.35 m per lane to the right of the centreline, so lane 3 of a 4-lane avenue sat 11.7 m off centre on a road whose half-width is 7.6 m
fix: Fit travel lanes inside the carriageway less its parking lanes, centred on the centreline for one-way and on the correct half for two-way
verification: Lane spacing now derives from LION's own streetwidth and number_park_lanes; no vehicle leaves the asphalt

title: Vehicles spawned inside one another
how_found: Counting pairs closer than their combined half-widths: dozens per frame
root_cause: Spawn picked a random position along a lane without checking occupancy, and car-following only resolves a gap on the frame after
fix: Reject a spawn whose position is within the combined half-lengths plus the minimum gap of an existing vehicle in that lane
verification: Overlaps fell from dozens to 0-14 out of ~400, and the remainder are cross-lane conflicts at junctions rather than spawn errors

title: 557 vehicles simulating and only 6 within 120 m; the camera's own street was empty
how_found: Instrumenting the SoHo shot after it rendered with no visible traffic
root_cause: Spawn lanes were picked uniformly from the simulation disc, and area grows with the square of the radius, so nearly every vehicle landed in the far ring
fix: Sort candidate lanes by distance and pick with a squared random index, which biases hard toward the camera
verification: Vehicles within 120 m rose from 6 to 60-69 across five camera positions

title: Every capture wrote a 0-byte PNG and still reported ok:true
how_found: Shooting the first street-life evidence set: six files, all 0 KB
root_cause: The canvas is sized from innerWidth, and a Browser pane that is not displayed reports 0, so the renderer had a 0x0 drawing buffer and toDataURL returned the six-character string "data:,"
fix: Capture pins its own 1280x720 render size and restores the viewport afterwards; the sink rejects a body under 1000 base64 characters with HTTP 422 instead of writing it
verification: Six shots re-taken at 171-525 KB each; an artificially emptied body now returns ok:false

title: An 8 m spruce standing on the pavement of Fifth Avenue
how_found: Looking at the first street-level capture
root_cause: The species-to-crown table put pyrus, prunus, malus and crataegus in the conifer bucket - Callery pear, cherry, crab apple and hawthorn, every one of them a small round-headed broadleaf
fix: Conifer form now contains only actual conifers; pear moved to the upright form, the other three fall through to spreading broadleaf
verification: Conifers fell from an implied 15% to 399 of 54214 trees (0.74%), and the genus ranking now matches the NYC street tree census: honeylocust, oak, ginkgo, Callery pear, linden

title: Walk-mode evidence shots were taken from inside a moving bus
how_found: Two of the first three street-level captures were filled by a dark mass at the camera
root_cause: Capture snapped walk-mode shots to the nearest drivable centreline, which stands the camera in the middle of the traffic lane
fix: Snap walk shots to the walk graph instead, and measure eye height from the pavement rather than the carriageway
verification: All six street-level shots now stand on the pavement at 13.9 m world height (12.0 land + 0.20 kerb + 1.7 eye)

title: Pedestrians walked into building walls and off the kerb
how_found: Raycasting straight down from 250 walkers and comparing the surface height with the pavement height
root_cause: The lateral offset was scaled by a sidewalk width estimated from the street width. Where the estimate ran wide, walkers on the building side entered the footprint and walkers on the kerb side stepped into the roadway
fix: 48_build_walk.py probes outward from every retained sample and stores the free half-width per vertex per side, measured off the sidewalk survey; the runtime scales the offset by the surveyed width at the walker's own position
verification: On-pavement rose from 92.2% to 98.7% of 300 sampled; walkers inside a building footprint fell from 2 in 250 to 0; lateral spread widened from 0.6 m to 4.2 m

title: 71% of walk lanes reported no room to stand on either side
how_found: Summarising the free-width distribution straight after adding it
root_cause: Each kept vertex took the minimum free width over the span it represented, and the simplifier drops eight vertices in nine, so one doorway alcove or pinched corner zeroed a whole block
fix: Use the low quartile over the span instead of the minimum, and exclude the samples the run bridged across a driveway, which are not pavement and read as zero
verification: Lanes with no usable width fell from 71.2% to 1.4%; 56.0% now have room on both sides

title: The crowd was a silhouette: every figure read as near-black
how_found: Looking at the SoHo capture
root_cause: The clothing palette was authored as dark greys between 0x1d and 0x5c. Those are sRGB values and three converts them to linear, so 0x2a2c30 lands at 0.023 - effectively black
fix: Rebalance the palette to roughly a quarter dark, a third mid and the rest light, which is what a midday pavement actually looks like
verification: Tops now span 0x1f2228 to 0xe2e0da; figures are legible against both the pavement and the shaded building wall

title: The pedestrian limb rig decoded every hip pivot to 3.08 m, above the top of the head
how_found: Decoding TEXCOORD_0 out of peds.glb before writing the shader
root_cause: glTF's UV origin is the opposite corner from Blender's, so the exporter writes 1 - v. The pivot height was authored as z/4 and arrived as 1 - z/4
fix: Decode the pivot as (1 - uv.y) * 4 in the vertex shader, with the flip named in the comment
verification: Hip pivots read 0.92 / 0.88 / 0.65 m for adult_a, adult_b and child, matching the authored figures

title: PLUTO floor areas and unit counts were being counted once per building on a lot
how_found: The busiest daytime cell in the derived demand field reported 3.3 million m2 of office space inside one 200 m block
root_cause: PLUTO describes a tax lot, and the registry copies its attributes onto every building matched to that lot. 20.6% of Manhattan buildings share a lot, and they are disproportionately the large ones
fix: Apportion every lot-level total across the buildings on the lot by approximate built volume (footprint x floors). Splitting evenly would put half a lot's offices in its loading dock
verification: Totals fell to the per-lot figures and match the real borough: 730806 residential units against about 870000 actual, 36.0 M m2 office against about 40 M, 129 M m2 floor area. Before the fix: 2095335 units, 57.8 M m2, 324 M m2

title: Times Square was quieter than a SoHo side street
how_found: Comparing the pedestrian count across the six evidence shots: SoHo 445, Times Square 243
root_cause: Crowd density scaled with how much pavement was in scope and traffic with how many lanes were, which measure street layout rather than activity. SoHo has more small streets per hectare than Midtown has
fix: Build a 200 m demand field from PLUTO retail, office and residential floor space, and weight both the spawn total and the per-lane spawn by it
verification: Pedestrians per walk lane now run 1.04 at Herald Square, 1.00 at 42nd and 6th, 0.41 in SoHo, 0.16 in the West Village, 0.11 in Inwood - a 9.5x spread in the right order. The field's own peak cells are Herald Square, Penn Station and Bryant Park

title: Traffic volume weights were compressed into a 0.23-0.38 band and changed nothing
how_found: Summarising the lane weight distribution after wiring the DOT counts in
root_cause: The weight normalised against the maximum segment volume. One segment of the FDR Drive carries 2700 vehicles an hour against a borough median of 57, so every ordinary street was squeezed against zero
fix: Normalise against the 90th percentile of edge volume (157.5 vph), emitted in the data file rather than hard-coded in the runtime
verification: Lane weights now span 0.07 to 1.00 with a median of 0.76

title: Vehicles were no more likely to be on an avenue than on a mews
how_found: Measuring the mean measured volume of occupied lanes against the mean of all lanes in scope: a ratio of 0.99 to 1.13
root_cause: Spawn acceptance was linear in the lane weight. With weights centred on 0.76 that runs 0.80 against 1.00 - a 1.2x preference, invisible against sampling noise
fix: Cube the acceptance probability and raise the spawn guard so the loop can still reach its target
verification: Concentration rose to 1.39x at Herald Square, 1.43x in East Harlem, 1.21x in SoHo. Modest and reported as modest; the DOT counts cover 564 of 11405 drivable edges and the fitted model for the rest is only slightly better than the mean

title: NYC DOT Bi-Annual Pedestrian Counts (2de2-6x2h) cannot be read from the public API
how_found: Attempting to fetch it as the independent validation set for the pedestrian demand field
root_cause: The dataset reports 114 rows but every column is hidden on the tabular endpoint: JSON returns 114 empty objects and CSV returns blank lines. It is Esri-backed, the same pattern as the map resources 3mf9-qshr and vfx9-tbb6
fix: Not fixable from here. The pedestrian field is therefore validated against known geography (its peak cells are Herald Square, Penn Station and Bryant Park) rather than against measured footfall, and DATA_SOURCES.md says so
verification: Confirmed on both .json and .csv endpoints and via $query=SELECT *. Re-confirmed wontfix 2026-08-05: external API, no action

title: The runtime had no LOD and no streaming: every tile was resident from anywhere on the island
how_found: Reading the streamer's own configuration while measuring the aerial views: far = 30000 on a 21 km island, resident 119 of 119 at every camera position
root_cause: 44_build_cells.py defined a five-tier ladder but nothing ever exported tiers 2 to 4, so the streaming radius was widened until the whole city fitted inside it. The docstring said so; nothing acted on it
fix: 56_build_lods.py exports L2, L3 and L4 massing per tile from the same frozen inputs Phase 1 used, and lod.js picks exactly one representation per tile per frame while the streamer hides that tile's own building meshes
verification: Times Square 2523015 -> 939647 triangles, 284 -> 89 draw calls, 0.55 -> 0.27 ms; downtown aerial 2695343 -> 832392 triangles, 341 -> 93 draws, 0.69 -> 0.27 ms. Resident tile payload 67.8 MB -> 10-16 MB

title: Flat 10-vertex massing rendered directly across the street from the camera
how_found: Only 1 to 2 tiles were reporting the full tier at street level, which is impossible if the near band is 900 m
root_cause: The tier was chosen from the distance to the tile's centre. A 1400 m tile has a 990 m half-diagonal, so a tile whose near corner is 200 m away measures 900 m from its centre and was handed to L2
fix: Measure to the tile's nearest edge instead, clamped per axis, using the tile's true grid extent rather than the centroid of the buildings inside it
verification: Tiles at full detail rose from 1-2 to 4-6 at street level; the visible near field is full facade geometry in every street-level capture

title: 85 of 101 far tiles never loaded any geometry at all
how_found: Counting LOD meshes actually present in the scene against the tier counts: 16 meshes for 101 tiles wanting one
root_cause: A tier load skipped because the in-flight cap was full was only retried when the tile's tier changed. For a tile that had settled on its tier, that never happened again
fix: Retry the load from the per-frame update whenever the wanted tier has no group and is not already in flight
verification: Missing tiers fell to 0 across four camera positions, verified by counting tiles whose wanted tier has a manifest entry but no loaded group

title: A single always-resident L4 skyline mesh would have z-fought every near tier
how_found: Working through the swap logic before wiring it: the tiers are coincident geometry by construction
root_cause: The ladder in 44_build_cells.py specifies L4 as one merged city silhouette. That cannot coexist with a per-tile swap - from Midtown you need L4 for downtown and full detail underfoot at the same time, and one mesh cannot be both
fix: Emit L4 per tile like the other tiers, so exactly one representation is on per tile at any range
verification: 5060 triangles over 42 tiles, 506 buildings at or above 100 m. No coincident geometry in any capture

title: The LOD tiers are built on the 1400 m tile grid, not the 800 m sector grid the ladder specifies
how_found: Deciding the swap unit while wiring lod.js
root_cause: The sector and tile grids do not nest: an 800 m sector straddles up to four 1400 m tiles. A distance-based swap between a sector proxy and a tile of full detail would either draw a building twice or leave a hole
fix: Build on the tile grid, which is the grid the full-detail geometry actually exists on, so each tile shows exactly one of full, L2, L3 or L4
verification: Verified by raycast: L2 roof heights match the registry's surveyed heights with median, p90 and max error all 0.00 m over 390 samples. Re-confirmed wontfix 2026-08-05: LOD_REPORT.json grid_m = 1400.0, design decision

title: 2,550 rain drops rendered and not one pixel of rain appeared
how_found: Counting drop instances inside the view frustum: 682 of them, and the capture showed nothing
root_cause: The rain and splash meshes were authored with COLOR_0 alpha 0, following the paint-mask convention used by the fleet and the props. Their runtime material is MeshBasicMaterial with vertexColors, and three multiplies COLOR_0's alpha into opacity when USE_COLOR_ALPHA is defined, so every drop was fully transparent
fix: Author rain and splash at alpha 1 and let the material's own opacity do the transparency. The clouds, authored at alpha 1, rendering correctly all along is what identified it
verification: Toggling rain with traffic and crowd frozen changes 204,223 of 230,400 pixels; drops are visible as streaks across the frame

title: Rain streaks were authored 6 mm wide, which is a third of a pixel
how_found: Working out why drops with correct positions were still not visible
root_cause: The streak width was chosen for physical plausibility. At a 62 degree field of view across 1280 pixels, one pixel is about 19 mm at 20 m, so a 6 mm streak covers 0.3 of a pixel
fix: Author at 36 mm, roughly two pixels at 20 m. Width here is set by the screen, not by physics
verification: Streaks are legible against both the sky and the building faces in the rain capture

title: Evidence captures of rain showed no rain even after the drops were fixed
how_found: Frustum-testing the drop instances immediately after a capture
root_cause: The rain volume follows the camera, and the capture hook stepped traffic and the crowd but not the weather, so the drops were still positioned around wherever the camera had been before the shot
fix: Step the weather in the capture hook alongside the other simulations
verification: 682 of 2,550 drops inside the frustum at capture time, and visible in the frame

title: The crowd murmur could not be switched off
how_found: Rendering the audio graph offline with every layer gain set to zero: it measured 0.0165 RMS instead of silence
root_cause: The swell oscillator was connected directly to the crowd layer's own gain AudioParam. An oscillator connected to a param is summed into it, so a gain of zero still swung between plus and minus 0.35
fix: Modulate a separate gain node in series instead, so the layer's own gain multiplies through it
verification: A mix with all layers at zero now measures exactly 0.00000 RMS; all seven audio assertions pass

title: At night the sun lit the undersides of every cornice in the city
how_found: Reading the sun vector out of the time-of-day table at 22:00: elevation -18 degrees
root_cause: The keyframe table carries real negative elevations at night, and a directional light below the horizon shines upward
fix: Floor the elevation used for the light direction at 3 degrees; the table's own intensity is what makes it night
verification: Sun intensity at 22:00 is 0.11 with the direction above the horizon

title: The umbrella mesh aborted the Blender build with "internal error setting the array"
how_found: Running 58_weather.py for the first time
root_cause: The canopy underside was the same triangles wound backwards. mesh.validate() removes reversed duplicates, so the per-loop colour array was 96 entries against 72 loops. Blender's own message names neither the mesh nor the cause
fix: Build the underside as a real second shell offset by 20 mm, and add an explicit length check in to_object that names the mesh and the number of dropped faces
verification: PROP_umbrella exports at 42 verts and 40 tris; the guard now fails loudly rather than as an internal error

title: Rebuilt asset glbs were silently not picked up in dev
how_found: A rebuilt weather.glb did not change the render, which is the same symptom as P2-021
root_cause: The world tiles carry an mtime in their URL for cache busting, but vehicles.glb, props.glb, peds.glb and weather.glb do not, and the /tiles/ mount is served with max-age 3600
fix: Append a timestamp query in dev builds only; production relies on file hashing
verification: A rebuilt weather.glb now takes effect on reload without clearing the browser cache

title: The first penthouse capture showed no room at all, only the view
how_found: Looking at the capture: a 464 m panorama with no floor, no ceiling and no glass in frame
root_cause: The camera offset and look direction were derived from the room's yaw by hand. The rooms are authored Blender-side as +x into the room, +y left, +z up, and the exporter remaps that to (x, z, -y) -- so the hand-written trig put the camera outside the building facing away from it
fix: Transform the eye, look target and doorway through the group's own matrix with a single local(bx, by, bz) helper that applies the Blender-to-glTF axis swap once, and enter with camera.lookAt rather than a computed yaw
verification: Camera inside the room bounding box and the room inside the frustum, asserted for all three rooms; the room is visible in every capture

title: The corner market was placed inside New 42nd Street Studios, which is a theatre
how_found: Printing the building each interior anchored to
root_cause: The anchor test used height and position only, so it took whatever low building was tallest in the search box
fix: Require a mixed_use_avenue, retail_podium or cast_iron_loft archetype as well
verification: The market now anchors to a mixed_use_avenue building; the penthouse independently picked Central Park Tower at 472 m and the lobby a 325 m tower

title: Every interior ceiling rendered pure black
how_found: The first framed penthouse capture: floor lit, ceiling absent
root_cause: The indoor fill is a HemisphereLight, whose sky colour lights up-facing surfaces and ground colour down-facing ones. A ceiling faces down, and the ground colour was 0x2a2622
fix: Warm the ground colour to 0xb9a894 and raise the indoor intensity; the luminous ceiling panels carry the rest through the emissive patch
verification: Ceiling and panels both read in all three interior captures

title: The HQ lift link to Floor 45 dangled and the HQ lobby was never placed
how_found: A console warning on boot: dangling link hq_floor45 -> hq_lobby
root_cause: hq.js built its room map from hq.glb alone, but the lobby it reuses is INT_lobby, which lives in interiors.glb
fix: Seed the map from the interiors loader's own mesh map, so an authored room can be stood up a second time somewhere else
verification: Both links resolve; the runtime reports rooms [hq_lobby, hq_floor45] and E rides the lift in both directions

title: The building the HQ stands on was invisible but still solid
how_found: Raycasting down through the HQ footprint to check what was under the tower: the hidden building answered at 112.4 m
root_cause: Suppression collapses vertices in the vertex shader, so the CPU geometry is untouched and every raycast still hits it. The filter that should have caught that missed too: Draco quantises _BID, so it decodes as 34686.0039 and the Map lookup for 34686 failed
fix: Round the decoded id, and route the walk collider and the building inspector through the same hitSuppressed() predicate
verification: Ray down the old footprint: top hit was bid 34686 at 112.4 m, now the ground at 12.0 m, 2 hits dropped; a neighbouring column drops 0

title: The walk collider pushed the player into buildings instead of out of them
how_found: A scripted walk straight at the HQ podium ended up 36 m inside the building
root_cause: _resolveWalls probed along the four world axes and pushed back along the probe axis rather than along the wall. Manhattan's grid is about 29 degrees off the world axes, so for nearly every wall in the city that push has a component along the wall -- measured at +0.48 m of forward travel per metre of push against the HQ podium
fix: Push along the hit face's world-space normal, falling back to the probe axis only when the face has none
verification: The same scripted walk now stops at local x 8.29 against a facade at 9.0, one body radius short; the open-street control still runs free

title: Every box in the authored asset library was wound inside out
how_found: Chasing P2-061: a front-side raycast at the podium wall passed through x=9 and hit x=46, and the face normal at 9 pointed +x, into the building
root_cause: Builder.box() listed its six faces with reversed winding. Signed volume of a 2 m cube came out -8 instead of +8. Backface culling then dropped every near face and left the viewer looking at the inside of the far one, which on a convex flat-shaded box is nearly invisible -- so it survived in five scripts covering the vehicle fleet, 112,418 props, the rain, three interiors and the HQ
fix: Reverse the six face tuples in all five copies of Builder.box() and re-export every asset
verification: Signed volume +8.0 after the fix; the podium face at x=9 is now a front-side hit with normal -x; the plaza capture visibly changes from the dark far wall to the pale stone that was authored

title: The HQ lobby looked at a wall instead of the street
how_found: The first HQ lobby capture: a glazed street wall with flat grey two metres beyond it
root_cause: The podium's entrance recess was authored as one solid block so it would read as a reveal from the plaza; the lobby is placed 0.6 m behind it, so the block sat between the lobby glass and the street
fix: Build the recess as real jambs and a head around a 20 x 7.2 m opening, with a threshold slab
verification: The lobby capture now shows the pavement, the buildings opposite, street trees and a pedestrian through the glass

title: Floor 45's glass briefing room rendered as an opaque grey box
how_found: The first Mission Control capture: a solid block in the middle of the operations floor
root_cause: Its two glass walls were authored into INT_floor45, which the runtime renders with the opaque room material; only meshes named GLAZE_* get the transparent one
fix: Move the two walls into GLAZE_floor45 and leave mullions behind in the shell
verification: The briefing room reads through in the Mission Control capture; GLAZE_floor45 went from 2 panes to 4

title: The HQ site picker chose the frontage street by segment midpoint
how_found: The first run reported a lot addressed on West 42nd Street as fronting West 41st
root_cause: nearest_street() compared the distance to each segment's midpoint. A long segment running past the front door has its midpoint half a block away -- the same mistake as P2-045, which picked an LOD tier by distance to the tile centre
fix: Project the point onto the segment and use the closest point on it
verification: The chosen lot's frontage is now the street its own footprint touches; yaw is emitted once at build time and the runtime uses it verbatim, so placement and suppression cannot disagree

title: The corridor could not route from the penthouse to the market
how_found: Boot log: 'no market route, 2.63 km to the HQ' -- one of two routes solved
root_cause: The route solver treated the graph's oneway field as a boolean. It is tri-state: 1 is a->b, -1 is b->a, 0 is both. Treating -1 as truthy sent 4,271 of the 11,395 drivable edges the wrong way and stranded whole neighbourhoods
fix: Add the a->b arc when oneway >= 0 and the b->a arc when oneway <= 0
verification: Both routes solve: 2,509 m driven against 2,252 m straight (ratio 1.11) to the market, 2,705 m against 1,851 m (1.46) to the HQ; 210 samples at 25 m spacing all sit 0.00 m from a drivable centreline

title: The lift ride showed open sky instead of the inside of a lift
how_found: The first descent capture: Manhattan from 450 m with a grey slab floating in it
root_cause: LIFT_cab's three solid walls were authored with inward=False, so they face out. A lift is only ever seen from inside, and from inside they were backface-culled
fix: Drop the flag; all three walls face in
verification: The descent capture now shows the cab, the car operating panel and the floor readout, with Central Park going past through the door gap

title: The lift ride faced whatever direction the previous leg left the camera in
how_found: The second descent capture: inside the cab, but nose-first into a corner
root_cause: The lift leg set the cab's position and the camera's position but never its orientation
fix: Aim at the doors and the floor indicator on entering the leg, and leave mouse-look free for the rest of the ride
verification: The capture faces the doors; the panel is in frame on the left

title: The driver's view was blacked out across the top quarter
how_found: The first driving capture: a solid black band over the windscreen
root_cause: The headlining, both roof rails, the mirror and the sun visors all ran forward past the windscreen header, overhanging the glass by 0.33 m and sitting between the eye and the road
fix: End the headlining and rails at the header, and move the mirror and visors behind it
verification: The windscreen aperture now reads from the bonnet to the buildings up the avenue; headroom over the driver's eye measured at 0.27 m

title: Mouse-look was pinned to the windscreen while driving
how_found: Reading the drive path: _driveAt re-aimed the camera at a point 30 m up the road on every frame
root_cause: Setting an absolute look direction per frame overwrites whatever the player did with the mouse in between
fix: Aim once when the leg starts, then apply only the car's yaw *delta* each frame, so the view turns with the car and the player can still look out of the side window
verification: The driving capture is taken with the default heading; turning the view during a leg now persists across frames

title: The corridor's final shot came back a flat colour
how_found: The arrival capture at Shenron: 1280x720 of uniform dark blue
root_cause: The camera was placed at dais x minus 5.6 m, which is room-local x = -0.8 -- outside Floor 45 and inside the tower's curtain wall
fix: Place it between the glazing and the dais, off to one side, so the form reads against the operations floor rather than against the window
verification: The arrival capture shows the form coiling above the dais with the consoles, the video wall and the city behind it

title: The car interior rendered as black cut-outs
how_found: The driving capture: dashboard and steering wheel silhouetted against a correctly lit street
root_cause: The cabin is lit only by the scene's sun, which reaches none of it; a real interior in daylight is full of bounce off the road and the buildings
fix: Raise the shared indoor fill to 0.62 for the driving legs, low enough that the city through the glass is still the bright thing
verification: Dash, wheel, door cards and seats all read in the driving capture

title: ODbL attribution was present but not reasonably findable
how_found: Auditing the release blocker: reading index.html and style.css rather than trusting that the line existed
root_cause: The notice named two of the eight datasets the world is built from, and was rendered at 11px with opacity .65 and pointer-events:none in the corner of a 3D scene. ODbL 4.3 asks for attribution a reader can actually find, and 'technically on screen' is not that
fix: Legible one-line notice with a working link, plus a full credits panel listing every dataset, its id and its licence, reachable with L or from the link. H no longer hides the notice
verification: Credit line reads 'Map data (c) OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 - NYC Open Data - MTA - data sources & licences'; the panel carries 9 dataset rows and the derivative-database statement

title: Subway kiosks from the same station stacked on top of each other
how_found: Measuring pairwise centre distances across all 658 placed kiosks
root_cause: A station complex publishes several entrances within a few metres of each other and each snapped to the nearest wide pavement independently, so nine pairs overlapped and two landed at exactly the same point
fix: After snapping, slide along the kerb line in 1 m steps until the kiosk clears every placed neighbour by 3.0 m; drop it rather than stack it if 12 m of sliding does not clear
verification: Overlapping pairs 9 -> 0, closest centres now exactly 3.00 m; 8 kiosks nudged, 0 dropped for clashing; 98.3% of centres still inside a surveyed sidewalk polygon

title: The runtime's start position was labelled Times Square and is not
how_found: A demand probe at the documented 'Times Square' coordinate returned 0 station entrances, which is impossible for that corner
root_cause: START was (-1900, -600), which is 40.7746 N 73.9905 W -- Lincoln Square, about 1.8 km up Broadway. Times Square is (-1476, -2433). Performance figures measured at the start position had been reported as Times Square numbers, and Times Square is the denser of the two views
fix: Move START to the real Times Square and name the constant, with the old value and why it mattered recorded in the comment
verification: The boot camera now opens at (-1476, -2433); the same probe returns 0.78 entrances per cell and demand 0.97

title: The ingest could not reach any dataset outside the city's own portal
how_found: Looking for subway entrances: the MTA publishes on data.ny.gov, and every id 404ed against data.cityofnewyork.us
root_cause: The Socrata host was baked into the BASE format string
fix: Let a dataset id carry its own host as 'host/id', defaulting to the city portal
verification: 868 Manhattan entrances fetched from data.ny.gov i9wp-a4ja in 2 s; the seven existing city jobs are unchanged

title: No permanent winding guard: the P2-062 inside-out fix corrected Builder.box() but added no assertion, so the same defect class could return silently
how_found: Reading the HANDOFF section-0 checklist against the five fixed scripts during the qa-integrity audit
root_cause: The fix verified signed volume once (+8.0 for a 2 m cube) but did not make the measurement a build gate, exactly what HANDOFF section 0 prescribes
fix: New scripts/mesh_audit.py (pure stdlib, no bpy import): signed_volume, is_closed, assert_outward (hard fail for exterior solids) and report_volume (diagnostic for interior shells). Wired into all 8 Builder.to_object() copies: hard assert in 52_vehicles, 54_props, 56_build_lods, 58_weather, 66_subway; diagnostic in 60_interiors, 62_hq, 64_corridor (rooms wind inward by design). Self-test: cube +8.0 / inverted -8.0 caught, open meshes skipped
verification: python scripts/mesh_audit.py --self-test -> pass:true. All primitives measured outward-wound: box 8.0, tapered box 4.667, tube 5.657, cone 1.886, blob 2.828 (all closed). All 8 authoring scripts still compile

title: Every doorway walk-in approached the wall 1.70 m to the side of its own opening
how_found: Booting the app headless and printing room.local(0,0,1.7) against group.localToWorld(0,0,1.7) for all six rooms; then tracing the walk frame by frame
root_cause: doors.js was written in the authored room frame (+x into, +y left, +z up) but fed those vectors straight to group.localToWorld, whose frame is (x into, y up, z along the wall). The Blender->glTF swap (x,y,z)->(x,z,-y) that interiors.place() keeps in room.local() was applied zero times, so 1.7 m up became 1.7 m sideways -- the same class as P2-056
fix: authToLocal/localToAuth cross the boundary once, in _local() and roomToWorld(); the door assembly gets the same swap as a single -90 deg rotation about x on its own child group (AUTHORED_ROT_X)
verification: The two readings differed by exactly 1.70 m of height on all 6 rooms. Before: camera pinned at room-local x = -0.721 m for 65 consecutive frames with the door fully open. After: 4/4 doorways crossed, walk-in max per-frame jump 0.157-0.161 m

title: The wall cut rebuilt its faces from fan indices used as vertex offsets, scattering geometry back across the opening
how_found: A collision probe cast from inside the home lobby at the stall point hit tile geometry at (u,v) = (0.00, 0.99) -- dead centre of a 2.2 x 2.5 m doorway that rays at other heights passed straight through
root_cause: cutWallInMesh built a fan index over a shared vertex list, then emitted triangles as [base+i, base+i+1, base+i+2] with i running over the fan values rather than its positions. The rebuilt faces referenced whatever vertices sat at those offsets. The pure cut math was unit-tested and correct; nothing tested the index bookkeeping
fix: Emit three fresh vertices per fan triangle and index them sequentially. Added three geometry-level tests that raycast the rebuilt mesh rather than checking polygons
verification: Doorcheck went from 0/4 to 3/4 passing on this fix alone. Opening probe blocked 0/15 rays at all four doorways; unit tests 26/26 including out-of-range index and area conservation (kept 234.5 m2 of a 240 m2 quad minus a 5.5 m2 door)

title: The glazed entrance wall was deleted rather than opened
how_found: Counting surviving triangles in each room glaze mesh after the cut
root_cause: _cutRoomGlass dropped every triangle whose AABB touched the door box. The lobby glaze is a single 24 m quad, so the whole pane went
fix: New cutGlazeRect does the same exact 2D rect subtraction the wall gets, in the glaze own (along-wall, up) frame, and only on faces within 0.5 m of the entrance plane
verification: Glaze triangles remaining 0 -> 6 (bodega) and 12 (the three lobbies); unit test asserts kept area equals pane minus door and no vertex sits strictly inside the opening

title: The door assembly was built lying on its side
how_found: Measuring the world AABB of the leaf and the lit ceiling panel
root_cause: Same authored-frame error as P2-078: the assembly boxes were built with the along-wall and up axes swapped
fix: The assembly hangs off a child group carrying AUTHORED_ROT_X; _assemblyMetrics() reports leaf height, leaf width and lit-panel height so the check needs no render
verification: Leaf 1.76 m tall / 2.36 m wide -> 2.36 m tall / 1.58 m wide; lit panel 0.17-1.83 m above the pavement -> 2.63 m above the floor

title: The HQ podium authored entrance recess is solid, and a door was placed on it
how_found: Rays into HQ_tower at 1 m spacing from -4 m to +4 m along the frontage, at four heights
root_cause: kind:recess skipped the wall cut entirely on the assumption the podium already had an opening, and RECESS_WALL_DIST hard-coded the podium front at 5.0 m. Measured, the front is solid at every sample and sits 0.4 m from the room origin, so the assembly and the crossing plane stood 4.5 m out in the open plaza with the real wall untouched behind them
fix: A recess is cut like any other wall. The tower is a standalone mesh with no _bid and its own transform, so the cut resolves the wall by ray and runs in the mesh own coordinates (_frameInMeshSpace)
verification: wallDist 5.0 assumed -> 0.40 measured; 6 podium faces cut; opening probe blocked 15/15 -> 0/15; walk-in crosses in 43 frames with max jump 0.157 m

title: Rooms were shifted away from their own frontage, so the doorway was cut into a wall the player never reaches
how_found: Re-measuring the wall distance from the room final position after the shift
root_cause: Three faults compounded: the shift moved the room along +doorDir, which points into the building; the rotation aligned the room to one candidate wall while the shift used a different one distance; and _findWall projected the door axis by stepping along the normal from a face centroid, which lands off the plane by the whole wall distance and wherever the nearest triangle happened to be
fix: Correct the projection to a true perpendicular foot; iterate rotate/re-resolve until the frontage settles (FRONTAGE_PASSES); shift along -doorDir; then resolve the final wall by ray from the room settled position and report the residual
verification: Post-shift distance to the cut wall: 16.99 m / 9.80 m / 5.39 m -> 0.350 m at all three wall doorways, exactly WALL_GAP

title: Walking out of a doorway launched the camera 2.6 m onto the door header
how_found: The reverse-traversal walk test max per-frame jump, with the surface underfoot recorded
root_cause: controls._groundBelow casts from a metre above the eye and returns the first hit, so a door header or lit ceiling panel overhead counts as ground; the caller then snaps the camera to it with no upward limit
fix: Skip hits more than one step above the feet and keep searching downward. STEP raised 0.55 -> 0.65 m because the HQ podium plinth the lobby doorway sits on measures 0.60 m and a doorway you cannot step up to is not a doorway
verification: Reverse-traversal max jump 2.595 m -> 0.161 m at the three wall doorways (0.623 m at the HQ, which is the step down off its plinth)

title: Squeezing through a doorway displaced the camera 0.98 m in one frame
how_found: The walk test max per-frame jump, recorded with the door state at that frame
root_cause: _resolveWalls runs four axis probes and each pushes up to the body radius; in a doorway they compound. Correct collision response, but a visible discontinuity
fix: Clamp the total per-frame wall correction to 0.35 m; a deeper overlap resolves over the following frames
verification: Walk-in max jump 0.979 m -> 0.161 m, against a 0.5 m budget

title: The automatic door had no sensor on the room side and opened too slowly to walk through
how_found: The door-cycle and reverse-traversal checks: the reverse walk never crossed in 181 frames, and the walk-in always met a quarter-open leaf
root_cause: The trigger volume spanned only the street side, 2.3 m out, against a 2.2 s slide. The player covers 2.3 m in 0.55 s, and a door that only senses the street shuts behind whoever walked in
fix: Trigger spans -5.0 to +2.6 m about the door plane; leaf travel 1.1 s open / 1.6 s close (1.6 m/s, about what a real automatic entrance does)
verification: Reverse traversal crossed=false in 181 frames -> crossed=true in 43; door cycle still opens twice and closes twice

title: The passage cut was a demolition, and it also blew out the exact cut it had just made
how_found: Counting what the sweep removed, and probing the market threshold for the adjacent school wall
root_cause: The sweep dropped every triangle whose AABB intersected the door box. In a merged tile mesh a neighbour wall quad runs ground to roof, so whole facades went -- and the four exact pieces around the fresh hole have AABBs touching the box too
fix: Same exact rect subtraction in the same wall frame, applied to other buildings faces only, inflated by 0.15 m so a non-parallel neighbour leaves no slivers, plus a containment sweep for faces that cannot be rect-subtracted. A depth band and a per-triangle AABB keep the cut local; without the band the wall frame is an infinite plane and punches phantom doorways down the block
verification: Market threshold probe blocked 15/15 -> 0/15 rays; passage cut 4 faces of the neighbouring school plus 1 contained triangle, and nothing else

title: The doorway collider used a stale world matrix, so an open door still blocked the player
how_found: Instrumenting the walk test wall probes: Mesh < leaf < authored on 160 of 181 frames with the door reading fully open
root_cause: update() moved the leaf but nothing pushed the change into its world matrix. Raycasting trusts matrices rather than updating them, and the QA harness freezes the render loop, so the collider saw the leaf where it was at boot
fix: updateMatrixWorld on the door group immediately after the leaf moves
verification: Walk-in inside=false in 181 frames -> inside=true in 43

title: --expansion overwrote the file the runtime reads
how_found: Reading 68_build_doors.py while preparing the expansion path
root_cause: Both modes wrote data/manhattan/doors/doors.json, so generating the entrance-treatment set would have handed the runtime ~660 entries with no interior behind them -- holes into solid buildings, and the phase gate bypassed by a command-line flag
fix: The expansion set writes doors_expansion.json with runtimeEnabled:false; doors.load() refuses any config carrying that flag, and an entry with no interior room cuts nothing
verification: doors.json still holds the 4 corridor doorways after an --expansion run; 631 subway-tranche entries written to the separate file, all with a measured frontage yaw

title: The approximately 660 expansion set was generated as 13,125 buildings
how_found: Counting the generator output against the HANDOFF figure
root_cause: The generator unioned the subway-adjacent buildings with every retail ground floor and reported the total under a heading quoting ~660
fix: Two tranches: subway (the HANDOFF number) by default, retail behind --include-retail, each row tagged
verification: 631 buildings within 30 m of one of the 658 entrances (284 at 20 m, 480 at 25 m, 1,053 at 40 m); retail ground floor 12,834; union 13,125
